sum: A short ridge trek from Kande through forest to High Camp, with a dawn climb to the 4,200 m viewpoint or the 4,500 m base camp below Mardi Himal and Machhapuchhre.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide matters most on the ridge above High Camp, where cloud can close in within minutes and the path is hard to follow under snow.

access: Kande is an hour by road from Pokhara on the Baglung highway. The trek ends at Siding in the Mardi Khola valley, where jeeps take about two hours to return to Pokhara on a rough track.

photo.a: Blue-roofed lodges at Mardi Himal High Camp sit on a grassy ridge below the sharp, snow-tipped summit of Machhapuchhre.
photo.c: High Camp on the Mardi Himal ridge, below Machhapuchhre

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
taxi or jeep between Pokhara and the trailheads (not in every package)

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, a taxi to Kande shared by two, and a jeep seat back from Siding
tips: Carry at least two litres of water on the forest days and the summit morning; sources between the camps are unreliable.
Take microspikes and warm gloves from November to March.
The Upper Viewpoint gives nearly the same view as base camp. Go on only if the sky is clear and you feel strong.
Lodges are basic above Forest Camp. Bring a sleeping bag and a power bank.
Carry cash from Pokhara; there is nowhere to get money on the ridge.

days.t: Drive to Kande, walk to Pitam Deurali
days.note: An hour of stone steps leads to the lawns of Australian Camp and the first full view of the range. The trail then follows the ridge through Pothana, where permits are checked, and climbs gently in forest to the lodges at Pitam Deurali.

n: New Lali Gurans guest house and restaurant

days.note: The Mardi trail leaves the main path and climbs the ridge through dense, mossy forest, with no village and little water between the lodge clusters. Lunch is at Forest Camp. The afternoon climbs more steeply to Low Camp, where Machhapuchhre appears at the head of the valley.

Within an hour the forest thins to scrub and the trail comes out on the open ridge at Badal Danda. From there it follows the crest, with steep drops on both sides in places, to High Camp. Arrive by lunch, drink plenty and rest for the early start.

days.t: Viewpoint and base camp, down to Low Camp
days.note: Start around four with a head torch. The path climbs the narrow crest for two to three hours to the Upper Viewpoint at 4,200 m, and base camp is another hour or more along the ridge. Turn round by nine at the latest, collect your bag at High Camp and carry on down to Low Camp.

days.t: Low Camp to Siding, drive to Pokhara
days.note: A steep forest descent of more than 1,100 m on a rough path, hard on the knees and slippery after rain. Have lunch in Siding, then take a jeep down the Mardi Khola valley to Pokhara, about two hours on a rough track.
